title: Deposit holds
prompt: The bank holds some deposits before the money can be spent. Write `solve(transactions)` so it returns `transaction_id`, `txn_type`, `channel`, `amount` and the `hold` each transaction gets.
rules: A deposit with a missing amount, or an amount of 0.00 or less, gets `review`.
Otherwise a deposit of 2500.00 or more gets `3_days`, and a `mobile` or `atm` deposit of 1000.00 or more gets `1_day`. Every other deposit gets `none`, including one with a missing channel.
A transaction that isn't a deposit (`txn_type` is not exactly `deposit`) gets an empty `hold` (null).
Return the five columns, in that order, for every transaction.
hints: The first true `when` wins, so the order is the rules' order: review, then 3 days, then 1 day, then none.
Put `F.col("txn_type") == "deposit"` into every condition with `&`, and leave out `otherwise`, so other types get `NULL`.

A missing amount makes every comparison untrue, so it can't match `<= 0`. Write the `none` rule as `amount < 2500` so it needs a real amount, then catch the deposits that are left with a final `when(is_deposit, "review")`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(transactions):
    # Return transaction_id, txn_type, channel, amount and hold.
    return transactions
explanation: Order is everything here. With `dep = F.col("txn_type") == "deposit"` and `amount = F.col("amount")`: `F.when(dep & (amount <= 0), "review").when(dep & (amount >= 2500), "3_days").when(dep & F.col("channel").isin("mobile", "atm") & (amount >= 1000), "1_day").when(dep & (amount < 2500), "none").when(dep, "review")`. The bad amounts come first, because -1200.00 is also below 2500.00 and would otherwise get `none`. A missing amount fails every comparison, so it falls past them all to the last `when(dep, ...)`. A missing channel fails `isin`, so a 1500.00 deposit with no channel reaches `none`, as the rules ask. There's no `otherwise`, so anything that isn't a deposit gets `NULL`. Writing the 1-day rule as "anything but branch" goes wrong twice: a deposit with no channel or a `system` channel would get `1_day` instead of `none`.
